title: J&K tightens rules for doctors seeking PG

ai.summary: J&K Health Department introduced stricter rules for doctors seeking postgraduate studies, requiring 5 years of service and at least 3 years of government service remaining after completion, with penalties for abandoning courses.

facts.claim: The J&K Health and Medical Education Department has introduced stricter eligibility conditions for in-service medical officers applying for No Objection Certificates (NOCs) to pursue higher studies.
facts.quote: Srinagar, Nov 16: The J&K Health and Medical Education Department has introduced stricter eligibility conditions for in-service medical officers applying for No Objection Certificates (NOCs) to pursue higher studies.

facts.claim: Doctors must have completed 5 years of service and have at least 3 years of government service remaining after completion of the course.
facts.quote: Doctors must have completed 5 years of service and have at least 3 years of government service remaining after completion of the course.

facts.claim: The order issued by Health and Medical Education Department (Circular No. 07-JK(HME) of 2026 issued on November 12) requires that the course must be their first such course during service.
facts.quote: The order issued by Health and Medical Education Department (Circular No. 07-JK(HME) of 2026 issued on November 12) requires that the course must be their first such course during service.

facts.claim: Doctors must have at least 3 years of remaining government service after completing the course, and those with less than 3 years left will not get an NOC.
facts.quote: Doctors must have at least 3 years of remaining government service after completing the course, and those with less than 3 years left will not get an NOC.

facts.claim: For tenure posts such as Senior and Junior Residency, Registrarship, demonstratorship, Fellowship, Tutorship within J&K, the prescribed probation or 3 years of service must be completed.
facts.quote: For tenure posts such as Senior and Junior Residency, Registrarship, demonstratorship, Fellowship, Tutorship within J&K, the prescribed probation or 3 years of service must be completed.

facts.claim: There is a compulsory 2-year “cooling-off period” which they will need to give in the department after returning from any study leave or tenure posting.
facts.quote: There is a compulsory 2-year “cooling-off period” which they will need to give in the department after returning from any study leave or tenure posting.

facts.claim: Abandoning a course midway or leaving before fulfilling obligations will attract penalties.
facts.quote: Abandoning a course midway or leaving before fulfilling obligations will attract penalties.

facts.claim: These include withholding of two increments.
facts.quote: These include withholding of two increments.

facts.claim: There is also a fine of Rs 2 lakh and the entire amount is paid during the course.
facts.quote: There is also a fine of Rs 2 lakh and the entire amount is paid during the course.

facts.claim: There is also a possibility of a ban on future government-sponsored courses.
facts.quote: There is also a possibility of a ban on future government-sponsored courses.

facts.claim: The department has invited applications from eligible officers of the J&K Health and Family Welfare (Gazetted) Service.
facts.quote: The department has invited applications from eligible officers of the J&K Health and Family Welfare (Gazetted) Service.

facts.claim: Applications must reach the respective directorates of health by 20 November 2026 for the 2027 cycle.
facts.quote: Applications must reach the respective directorates of health by 20 November 2026 for the 2027 cycle.

facts.claim: These rules build on earlier guidelines.
facts.quote: These rules build on earlier guidelines.

facts.claim: However the study-leave qualifying service has been raised from 3 to 5 years.
facts.quote: However the study-leave qualifying service has been raised from 3 to 5 years.

facts.claim: The officials said that the order aims to ensure doctors complete courses and return to serve in the J&K health system.
facts.quote: The officials said that the order aims to ensure doctors complete courses and return to serve in the J&K health system.

facts.claim: That, they said, may help in addressing the shortages in government facilities.
facts.quote: That, they said, may help in addressing the shortages in government facilities.
